metadata.title: Make Fun String Art using the Pegboard Frame from We R Memory Keepers
metadata.description:
The Organization Gallery from We R Memory Keepers is great for adding custom organization to your craft space.  Watch as Aly Dosdall uses the Pegboard Frame to create some fun wall decor to add in her Organization Gallery wall in her craft space!

This pegboard is an easy, already painted, framed, and ready-to-hang piece of decor!

nodes.plm_action: Thread blue yarn through top holes of frame to create diamond shape
nodes.plm_caption:
The video features a woman making a display on a peg board and using a set of strings for decoration.
The woman can be seen demonstrating how to create a diamond shaped design using the string.  The woman starts by placing a small roll of string on the table and begins unrolling it.  She then places it in a frame.  Once placed, she starts pulling it, creating triangles in a diamond shape, at which point she attaches it to a pegboard and places it over a brown piece of paper with a large dot pattern.  Finally, the woman creates an identical diamond pattern on the pegboard and runs it over the frame.

There are 2 frames in the video, 1 of which is open to show the front view, while the other is covered in white paper.  The second frame shown features a diamond shaped decoration pattern over the pegboard and brown back paper.  The background of the video is a white counter top with a grey wood wall.  On the counter are various art pieces that may be part of the supplies, or be on display.  The woman is standing behind the counter.  She wears a gray long sleeved shirt and floral apron.  The roll of string is light blue.  The frame and the brown paper are white and brown, respectively.  The pegboard is large and square, with a brown back.  Scissors are gold with a yellow handle.  Three small potted plants sit on a shelf on a grey brick wall.  These wall decorations also include white framed items that display art.  A clear glass container filled with something sits on the right of the wall frame and white writing with the brand and website is visible.  A coffee maker and blue and white striped tray sits behind the woman to the right.

summary.brief: Aly creates a diamond‑shaped string‑art design on a pegboard.
summary.detailed: Aly introduces the project, removes the paper backing from the back of the pegboard frame with a craft knife, and places a sheet of grid paper on the board to plan a diamond shape. She locates the central hole (hole 7 of 13) and threads a length of light‑blue yarn through the back, pulling it to the front and taping the end so it is hidden. Counting holes, she guides the yarn up, down and diagonally to trace the outline of the diamond, taping each segment to keep the yarn flat and concealed. After completing the outline, she adds additional yarn pieces to fill the interior facets of the diamond, again securing them with tape and trimming any excess with scissors. She flips the board to show that the back is tidy and the front displays a clean diamond pattern, then presents the finished piece and notes that the same method can be used for other shapes such as hearts or letters.

action.detailed: Thread light‑blue yarn through the pegboard holes to outline and fill a diamond shape, securing each segment with tape and trimming any excess yarn.

summary.brief: Ally crafts a diamond‑shaped string‑art design on the pegboard by threading yarn through its grid.
summary.detailed: After removing the back paper, Ally selects the central hole (hole 7) and pushes a length of yarn from the back side to the front. She pulls the yarn upward three holes, then down through the next hole, and continues alternating back‑and‑forth to trace the outline of a diamond across the pegboard grid. Once the outline is complete, she threads additional yarn strands to fill the interior facets of the diamond, keeping each strand taut. Throughout she places masking tape over the front to hide any yarn that might show through the holes, then flips the board, tapes off the loose ends, trims the excess yarn with scissors, and adjusts the tape so no yarn is visible on the opposite side. Finally she showcases the finished diamond string‑art piece.

action.detailed: Thread yarn through the pegboard holes to outline and fill a diamond shape, secure the yarn ends with masking tape, and trim any excess yarn.

summary.detailed: The video opens with Ally introducing the project and explaining that the pegboard’s back is covered with a removable paper backing. She cuts the paper away with a craft knife and sets it aside to expose the board’s rear side. Using a sheet of grid paper she sketches a diamond design to map the pattern. summary_sent_to_llm.description:
The Organization Gallery from We R Memory Keepers is great for adding custom organization to your craft space.  Watch as Aly Dosdall uses the Pegboard Frame to create some fun wall decor to add in her Organization Gallery wall in her craft space!

This pegboard is an easy, already painted, framed, and ready-to-hang piece of decor!
summary_sent_to_llm.root_summary: Aly introduces the project, removes the paper backing from the back of the pegboard frame with a craft knife, and places a sheet of grid paper on the board to plan a diamond shape. She locates the central hole (hole 7 of 13) and threads a length of light‑blue yarn through the back, pulling it to the front and taping the end so it is hidden. Counting holes, she guides the yarn up, down and diagonally to trace the outline of the diamond, taping each segment to keep the yarn flat and concealed. After completing the outline, she adds additional yarn pieces to fill the interior facets of the diamond, again securing them with tape and trimming any excess with scissors. She flips the board to show that the back is tidy and the front displays a clean diamond pattern, then presents the finished piece and notes that the same method can be used for other shapes such as hearts or letters.
